content: While looking into translating some proofs in weakestpre.v I noticed that we don't have an iloeb or equivalent tactic to Iris Rocq's iLöb. I found this issue which talked about implementing it, but which was closed by the author not long after. I was wondering if there had been a discussion already before about whether to implement the tactic or not, or if there was someone already working on it

iLöb is one of the tactics still missing. The tracking issue is here. No one is currently working on it at the moment. If you need it and don't want to wait on the implementation, you can usually apply the loeb_weak lemma directly to a goal of suitable shape to get the effect of iLoeb.

I was actually thinking whether to go on a sidequest and work on it. Thanks for pointing out the tracking issue, I need to get into the habit of checking those more directly. I think I'll try working on it for now
Great! Feel free to ping me if you have any questions about the proofmode.

I finished the my PR for the iloeb tactic. Althought I have marked the PR as "ready for review", I am not sure I'm satisfied with the final state of the code. In particular, I used functions defined for other tactics, such as irevert, iintro, iapply and imodintro, but I'm not sure whether the way I composed them is the most preferable way. I make use of a custom getMainGoal function to retrieve the MVarIds out of the ProofMode.State's goals field, which I'm not sure is something I am expected to do.

Another restriction of the current implementation is that it may change the order of hypothesis. I didn't think this was too much of an issue, but if it's undersirable I imagine adding a irevert IH; iintro #IH at the end of the tactic would suffice. Lmk if you think this makes sense.
Great, thanks for the PR! I hope to find some time to review this soon (hopefully).
